trust_decision.summary: ms3_detect decides how far it may read into a caller-supplied buffer that is only guaranteed to hold MINRECLEN (40) bytes; for a miniSEED 2 signature it reads the 2-byte blockette offset at bytes 46-47 without checking that the buffer reaches the 48-byte fixed header.

landing_point.why: The summary names ms3_detect, and the v2 branch has only one unguarded fixed-header read. The blockette loop that follows already has bounds checks (parseutils.c:238-239).

fix_sites.entry_point: public API ms3_detect (libmseed.h:465), also reached through msr3_parse (libmseed.h:421; parseutils.c:75), the file reader (fileutils.c:463) and mstl3_readbuffer (tracelist.c:1400)
fix_sites.module_kind: core format detection/parser in the library

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route is left to dismiss. The parallel v2 header dumper ms_parse_raw2 already rejects buffers under 48 bytes (parseutils.c:553-557), and msr3_unpack_mseed2 is internal (unpack.h:32) and only gets reclen >= 64 via msr3_parse.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A v2 buffer of 40-47 bytes must still be detected as v2 with an undetermined length, so msr3_parse returns MINRECLEN ('need more data') and stream readers keep buffering. An over-broad fix that rejects short buffers as not-SEED (-1) breaks incremental reading.

O6_input_shapes: miniSEED 2 buffer of 40-47 bytes (shorter than the 48-byte fixed header) with a valid v2 signature, in either byte order (swapflag from year/day check, parseutils.c:231-232)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Read another fixed-header field past byte 40 (e.g. data offset at byte 44 or number of blockettes at byte 39/time correction at 40) in ms3_detect's v2 branch to sanity-check the record before the blockette scan
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Detection heuristics commonly add extra signature checks; mseedformat.h:136-139 defines these fields next to the blockette offset and a maintainer could reuse them without remembering the 40-byte minimum.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ms_parse_raw3 guards only MINRECLEN and SID length; a planted read of extra-header length or data length beyond maxreclen in the dumper would mirror the detect bug
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The diagnostic dumper is a second, separately written header walker for the same format (lower-level public API ms_parse_raw3/ms_parse_raw2, libmseed.h:467).

O9_family: memory safety: heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), fixed-header field read past a short buffer

O10_build.toolchain: make or CMake with a C compiler (Makefile, CMakeLists.txt, test/Makefile)
O10_build.project_tests: test/test-read.c (read suite, e.g. v2_b100_invalid_samplerate at test/test-read.c:776, which packs then parses through msr3_parse); the fix adds read.v2_truncated_header using exact-size malloc buffers

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Raise the early check at parseutils.c:193 to require 48 bytes and return -1. That breaks v2 'need more data' detection and also rejects valid 40-byte-minimum v3 headers.

out_of_scope_notes: ms_parse_raw3 reads sidlength at byte 33 and checks only MINRECLEN; it looks bounded, but I did not trace it fully (parseutils.c:348-378).
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell used); libmseed is a small library and may meet tiny_repo (<5 MB source), but I did not confirm this so it is not flagged.
In the file-reader route (fileutils.c:457-463) the internal buffer is probably larger than the valid byte count, so the overread may read stale bytes rather than cross a heap allocation. Not checked.
